Mr. Md. Ratiqul Islam Mehedi with Mr. Md. Humayun Bashar, Advocate -- For the Petitioners 
Mr. M. Quamrul Haque Siddique, Advocate -- For the Opposite Party No.1
parties:
Md. Sayedul Haque and others ----- Defendants-Petitioners
Versus
Most. Nazma Begum ----- Plaintiff-Opposite Party
full_judgment:
Mr. A. N. M. Bashir Ullah, J:- This Rule on an application under Section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure (in short, the Code) at the instance of the defendants-petitioners was issued calling upon the opposite party No.1 to show cause as to why the judgment and decree dated 11.04.2007 passed by the learned Joint District Judge. 2" Court, Sherpur in Title Appeal No.106 of 2004 allowing the appeal and reversing the judgment and decree dated 30.09.2004 passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Nokia in Other Class Suit No.01 of 2003 dismissing the suit should not be set aside and/or pass such other or further order or orders as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

2. The facts leading to the issuance of the Rule, in short, is that the opposite party no. 1 Most. Nazma Begum as plaintiff instituted the above number title suit in the Court of Senior Assistant Judge, Nokia, Sherpur for recovery of the schedule land of the plot removing the structure thereon contending, inter-alia, that the suit land along with some other lands of mouza Kaida and Bazardi of hal Police Station Nokla former Nalitabari originally belonged to Kosor Maraud Parai, the father of the plaintiff who gifted 5.47 acres of land by a deed of Hebabill ewaz on 22.02.1972 and registered on 13.07.1972 to his 5 daughters including the plaintiff. 

3. By an amicable arrangement amongst the 5 sisters. The plaintiff got 1.10 acres of land through the said Hebabil ewaz. The plaintiff erected a house in the land of plot No.50 of settlement khatian no.I 08 and while she was living with her mother in the said house and she got married with her husband. 

4. The plaintiff engaged Abdus Samad Parai father of the defendant Nos.1-4 and predecessor of defendant Nos.5-7 the cousin for borga cultivation of .95 acres of land. In the month of Choitra, 1389 B.S the husband of the plaintiff has been serving in the Army of Bangladesh. Thus, the plaintiff himself was looking after the lands. When the plaintiff came to look after her lands, the defendant Nos.1-4 the predecessor of defendant Nos.5-8 Md. Abdus Samad Parai fraudulently created a Hebabil ewaz dated 23.10.1983 in the name of defendant Nos.1- 4 and Hafizul Haque predecessor of defendant Nos.5-8 and the defendant disclosing that the said Hebabil ewaz denied to make payment of the crops to the plaintiff. 

5. The plaintiff under the prevailing circumstances filed Other Class Suit No.26 of 1985 in the Court of Assistant Judge, Nokia against defendant nos.l-8 and Abdus Samad Parai and the said suit was decreed on contest on 26.04.1986 and against the said judgment and decree the defendants filed Title Appeal no. 63 of 1986 in the Court of District Judge, Jamalpur. Later on, the appeal was transferred in the Court of District Judge, Sherpur and was renumbered as Title Appeal no. 10 of 1988. During the pendency of the appeal Hafizul Haque the predecessor of defendant nos. 5-8 died as appellant no.2. As such, the appellate Court belw passed an abatement order on 05.04.1989. The defendant nos. 1-4 and the heirs of Hafizul Haque filed Miscellaneous Case no. 9 of 1980 under Order 9 Rule 4 of the Code for setting aside the abatement order but the said proceeding was dismissed on contest on 07.05.1999 and as against the said order the defendants filed Civil Revision no. 1839 of 1990 in the High Court Division. The High Court Division making the Rule absolute in the said revision by its judgment and order dated 03.11.1997 set aside the abatement order dated 07.05.1999 with a direction to rehear the Miscellaneous Case No.16 of 1989 for setting aside the abatement order and during the pendency of the said miscellaneous case in the Joint District Judge, I" Court, Sherpur, but the said miscellaneous case was dismissed for default on 27.01.2000. Thereafter, the appellate Court sent the record of the suit to the Court of Assistant Judge, Nokia, Sherpur and on a prayer dated 13.04.2000 filed by the plaintiff of that suit, the Court by its order dated 05.07.2000 sent the order of the Court to the concerned Sub-Registry Office to record the order of cancellation of the Hebabil ewaz dated 23.10.1983. 

6. When the plaintiff was taking preparation for getting the land back, the defendant Nos.1-8 dispossessed the plaintiff erecting tin shed and wooden house in the suit land on 27.08.2000. The plaintiff having been tried to resist them failed. When the Other Class Suit No.26 of 1985 and the subsequent proceedings arose out of the said suit were pending in the Courts for verdict, the defendants in order to create some cumbersome on the title of the plaintiff created as many as 8 deeds but all those deeds are collusive, fraudulent, motivated and illegal, hence the suit. 

7. The suit was contested by the defendant Nos.l-4 who filing written statement denying the materials allegation made in the plaint. The case of the defendants are, in short, is that the plaintiff is out of possession from the date of execution of Hebabil ewaz dated 23.10.1983 and from then the plaintiff is nobody for the suit land. Thus the plaintiff has filed the present suit after 19 years 2 months and 7 days. The defendants have acquired title by adverse possession from 23.10.1983. Since the plaintiff is out of possession from 1983 the suit is not maintainable at her instance. The plaintiff is a shrewd and cunning woman who at the instance of others have filed the suit for illegal gain. Abdus Samad Parai the predecessor of the defendant was a man of choice and solvate. He did not plough his own land and borga cultivate the land of others. He did not also borga cultivate the land of the plaintiff. The vexatious suit of the plaintiff is liable to be dismissed with costs. 

8. Upon the above pleadings, the trial Court framed as many as 6 issues to dispose of the suit. They examined 3 witnesses while the defendant examined 3 witnesses and both the parties filed some documentary evidences which were duly marked as exhibits in the suit. The trial Court upon considering of the evidence on record dismissed the suit that the suit is barred by limitation and as against the said judgment the plaintiff preferred title appeal in the appellate Court below and the said Court after hearing both the parties allowed the appeal holding that the suit is not barred by limitation and thereupon he decreed the suit in favour of the plaintiff. The defendant-petitioners being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the said impugned judgment of the appellate Court below moved this Court and obtained the present Rule. 

9. Mr. Md. Rafiqul Islam Mehedi with Mr. Md. Abul Bashar, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the defendant-petitioners supports the Rule and he sought to impeach the judgment and decree of the appellate Court below on the following four fold arguments.

10. Firstly, he submits that the suit was hopelessly barred by limitation as the plaintiff was ousted from the suit land on 23.10.1983 when she executed the Hebabil ewaz in favour of the defendants. Thereupon she could not come back into the possession of the suit land and the plaintiff filed the suit on 02.01.2003 that is almost after 19 years 3 months and 7 days of her dispossession. So, the defendants have acquired good title into the suit land by their such adverse possession and since the plaintiff could not file the suit within 12 years from her dispossession in 1983 as prescribed in Article 144 of the Code, the suit is hopelessly barred by limitation under section 28 of the Limitation Act. But the appellate Court below without appreciating this fact and circumstances wrongly came to a conclusion that the suit is not barred by limitation. He also submits that the plaint itself discloses the fact that after the disposal of the former Other Class Suit no. 26 of 1985 the plaintiff was taking steps for getting the land back from the defendants and this fact reveals the dispossession of the plaintiff from the suit land. He also submits that the date of dispossession as ventilated in the plaint on 27.08.2000 is an imaginary date which has been introduced for creating a cause of action for the present suit. Since the suit was not filed within 12 years from the date of dispossession, the plaintiff is not entitled to get any decree and relief in the suit. 

11. Secondly, he submits that the plaintiff has been claiming the suit land relying on the deed of gift dated 22.02.1972 reportedly executed by her father. But all the lands of the said deed of gift is situated within the Nokia Police Station but the said deed of gift was executed and registered at Mymensingh Sadar Sub-Registry Office. So, no title was passed in favour of the plaintiff through the said Hebabil ewaz as such the plaintiff did not acquired title into the suit land. 

12. Thirdly, he also submits that the correct identity of the land has not been given in the plaint though there appears some khatian nos. and plot nos. as to the description of the land but there is nothing in the record to show that which survey attract the said khatian and plot nos. So, this type of identity is vague and indefinite and upon relying such vague and indefinite identity of land there is a. little scope for giving possession to anybody else. 

13. Fourthly and lastly he submits that the plaintiff has filed the suit for recovery of khas possession for an area of .90 acres of land as described in the schedule of the plaint. In the first schedule, there is a description of .30 acre of land from plot No.68 of khatian no.10 of mouza Kaida. But the deed of gift dated 22.02.1972 will go to show that the father of the plaintiff gifted only .20 acres of land to his 5 daughters from the land of plot no.68 of khatian no.10. So, the plaintiff cannot claim .30 acres of land from plot no.68 of khatian no.10 and the Court will not a pa'ss decree for the land where apparently the plaintiff has no right, title and possession. Thus, he referring the above points and arguments submits that the trial Court rightly dismissed the suit holding that the suit was barred by limitation. But the appellate Court below on some erroneous view came to a wrong finding and conclusion that the suit is not barred by limitation. So, the judgment of the appellate Court below is liable to be set aside restraining that of the judgment passed by the trial Court. 

14. On the other hand, Mr. M. Quamrul Haque Siddique, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the opposite party no.1 opposing the Rule submits that the suit is not barred by limitation and the defendants did not acquire title into the suit land by adverse possession. He categorically submits that the defendants were claiming their possession into the suit land from 1983 relying, on the fraudulent and collusive Hebabl ewaz dated 23.10.1983. But the said Hebabil ewaz have been declared illegal by the trial Court in Other Class Suit no. 26 of 1985 and the said judgment was upheld and confirmed in that Title Appeal being no. 63 of 1986 and the said proceeding continued till 05.07.2000 and the trial Court and the appellate Court in that suit found the possession of the plaintiff into the suit land whereupon the Hebabil ewaz reportedly executed by the plaintiff in favour of the defendants was cancelled and the same was also noted in the volume of the deed. So, for any view of the matter the defendants cannot claim their possession into the suit land from 1983 to 2000 and the very claiming of the possession of the defendants in to the suit land during this period that is 1983 to 2000 is against the law as their possession has not been found in the former suit. 

15. He also submits that the defendants ousted the plaintiff from the suit land on 27.08.2000 erecting some houses on the suit land with the notice of all concerned and this type of hostile and notorious position can only be the counted as the date of beginning of adverse possession. So, from the date of dispossession of the plaintiff on 27.08.2000, the suit has been filed within 12 years as prescribed in Article 144 of the Limitation Act. So, in computing the time it will be resulted that the suit has not been filed within 3-years from the dispossession of the plaintiff. So, the suit is not hit under Section 28 and Article 144 of the Limitation Act. 

16. He next submits that the defendants-plaintiff at this stage raised question as to the registration of the deed of gift by the father of the plaintiff in 1972 in the District Sub-Registry Office, Mymensingh. But this fact was not raised in the Court below. As such, the plaintiff could not show any evidence of this point. Since this is a purely question of fact as to whether the District Registrar, Mymensingh had the jurisdiction to entertain such a deed of a police station under that district cannot ascertain at this moment. More so, the plaintiff acquired title into the suit land through the deed of gift by her father in the year 1972 and the defendant admitting the title of the plaintiff in to the suit land created Hebabil ewaz on 23.10.1983. So, at this stage of the proceeding the defendants cannot deny the title of the plaintiff on the strength of the deed of gift in 1972. In fact, the defendants in order to take some undue advantage have been using this point only. 

17. He also submits that it is not comet to say that the identity of the survey related with the khatian and plot numbers of the suit land have not been given in the plaint. He referring the plaint submits that the khatian and plot numbers are related with the settlement khatian. In this connection he also submits that when the first record of right was started under the provision of Bengal Tenancy Act in some of the area of our country. The first record of right is known as C.S record of right, that is, Cadstale Survey and in some district the same survey is known as settlement khatian. In the area of Mymensingh the first survey is know as settlement khatian and the same has been given in the pleadings. He candidly admits that it is fact that in the schedule of the plaint there is no identity of the survey and the same should have been there and if it would have been their, their would have no scope to create any confusion and unwanted debit on this fact. 

18. He also submits that in the record of right there appears no name of the concerned survey. After C.S. record of right in many area of our country revisional survey, that is, R.S. record of right and after coming operation of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act the S.A record of right has been prepared but in no record of right, the name of the survey has been articulated by the authority. So, it is not a ground for disbelieving the case of the plaintiff. 

19. He also submits that it is fact that the father of the plaintiff had gifted .20 acres of land from plot no.68 of khatian no.10 of mouza Kaida but the plaintiff has been claiming .30 acres of land from the said plot number. In this connection he argued that the defendants are nobody but the co-sharers of the plaintiff, thus the by an amicable arrangement among the co-sharers has been possessing .30 acres of land from the plot no.68 of khatian no.10 and since from the said particular land the plaintiff was ousted by the defendants, the same has been included in the schedule of the plaint.

20. In his concluding submission he submits that the appellate Court below did not commit any error of law rather considering the pros and cons of the suit decreed the suit rightly. So the decree passed by the appellate Court below should not be interfered by this Court. The appellate Court below of the right assessment of the evidence, fact and low involved there to rightly found that the suit is not barred by limitation and decreed the suit accordingly. So, the rule is liable to be discharged with costs. 

21. I have considered the above submissions and arguments of the learned Advocates of both the parties with profound attention and have gone through the materials on record. 

22. On going to the materials on record it appears that amongst the questions of limitation is the burning question in the suit. Most of the arguments of the learned Advocate for the petitioners are convergent to the fact of limitation. The plaintiff has asserted in the suit that on 27.08.2000 the defendants erecting tin shed and wooden house in the suit land dispossessed her. On the other hand, the plain case of the defendants is that from 1983 when the plaintiff executed Hebabil ewaz in favour of the defendants on 23.10.1983 for the suit land defendants have been possessing the suit land on the strength of the said Hebabil ewaz and from then the plaintiff is out of possession. 

23. From the materials on record it appears that this plaintiff filed Other Class Suit No.26 of 1985 in the competent civil Court for declaration that the Hebabil ewaz dated 23.10.1983 allegedly executed by the plaintiff in favour of Abdus Samad Parai has not been executed by her and the said suit was decreed on contest and the said judgment was alleged in an appeal being Title Appeal no.63 of 1986, later on the same was re-numbered as Title Appeal no.10 of 1988 but the appeal was abated on 05.04.1989 and a Miscellaneous Case being No.I6 of 1989 under Order 22 Rule 9 of the Code of Civil Procedure for setting aside the abatement order was tiled. But the said miscellaneous case was dismissed on contest on 07.05.1990. Against that order the defendants preferred Civil Revision being no.1839 of 1990 in the High Court Division and the Rule was made absolute on 03.11.1997 restoring the Miscellaneous Case no.16 of 1989 for rehearing. But after restoration of the said miscellaneous case the same was again dismissed on 27.01.2000. Thereafter, the defendants did not take any further step and ultimately the decree passed in Other Suit no.26 of 1985 remain intact till now. 

24. The defendants have been claiming heavily that the plaintiff has been dispossessed from the suit land on 23.10.1983 when she executed the Hebabil ewaz in favour of the defendants. Now, the question before me whether if for the sake of argument it is conceded for a moment that the plaintiff was dispossessed on 23.10.1983 whether this sought of dispossession can be considered as adverse possession of the defendants. 
25. Now, let us have a look-what is adverse possession in the eye of law. In the case of Secretary of State for India vs Devendra Lal Khan reported in 61 I A.78=38 C W N.. 285, the Privy Council laid down what constitutes adverse possession and observed in the following ways: "As to what constitutes adverse possession, a subject which formed the topic of some discussion in the case, their Lordships adopt the language of Lord Robertson in delivering the judgment of the Board in Radhamoni Devi Vs Collector of Khulna" (27 I.A. 136), where his Lordship said that the possession required must be adequate in continuity, in publicity and in extent to show that it is possession adverse to the competitor . It is sufficient that the possession should be overt and without any attempt at concealment so that the person against whom time is running ought, if he exercises due vigilance, to be aware of what is happening." 

26. The jest of the adverse possession as observed by the Privy Council is that the possession must be continuous having knowledge to others and it must have an expose against the real owner. In my consideration, the written statement of the defendants and their claim of possession in to the suit land from 1983 through the deed of Hebabil ewaz allegedly executed by the plaintiff is sufficient to hold that the possession of the defendants from 1983 is not any adverse possession at all rater the possession that have been claimed by the defendant themselves is based on the so-called deed of gift and this sort of possession can never be adverse possession against the real owner. 

27. Adverse possession is something as described by the Privy Council that it must be publicity to the all and adverse to the competitor. The case of the defendants that they are in possession of the suit land from 1983 is founded on the basis of the so-called Hebabil ewaz which has been cancelled subsequently. So, how this sought of possession can be manifested as adverse possession. The defendants having been claiming their possession heavily into the suit land from 1983 not by way of adverse possession but relying on the deed of gift which runs as follows:“বাদীর আরজির ৩নং দফার বর্ণিত ও স্বীকৃত মতে আরজির লিখিত ইং ২৩/১০/৮৩ বাংলা ১৩৯০ সনের ৫ইং কার্তিক তারিখের ৬৫৭৬ নং দলিলের দ্বারা উক্তরুপ ইং ১৯৮৩ সন হইতে মোকদ্দমা সংকান্ত দাবীর ভূমি হইতে বাদীনী নিঃস্বত্ববান দখল সংশ্রবহীন।”
If this is the dazzling case of the defendants as to their possession which is the crux point of the suit land, can their possession be considered as adverse possession. Adverse possession must be always hostile and notorious against the real owner. But the possession as claimed by the defendants into the suit land from 1983 was not hostile on notorious, rather/the same was founded on the so-called deed of gift dated 23.10.1983. Although, in my consideration after the judgment of the former suit the defendants cannot claim any right, title and possession in to the suit land on the basis of deed of gift dated 23.10.1983. But even then they showing their disrespect to the law as well as to the judgment of the former suit have been claiming their possession in to the suit from 23.10.1983. The assertion of possession of the defendants from 1983 on the basis of the deed of gift is a boomerang as to their case of adverse possession. 

28. The possession of the defendants in to the suit land if it is conceded for a moment from 23.10.1983 that would not come under the purview of adverse possession. The possession of the defendants in to the suit land from 1983 is not adverse possession in the eye of law rather the same was based on a deed of gift. The case of the plaintiff is that the defendants was inducted in to possession of the land in 1983 as her borgader while the definite case of the defendants that they have been possessing the suit land on the basis of Hebabil ewaz. If the case of the defendants are taken in to consideration in that case also their such possession is not adverse possession against the plaintiff, the real owner of the suit and they did not raised the pica of adverse possession at any point of time before filing of the present suit in the year 2003. 

29. In the case of Abdus Samad and others Vs. Deputy Commissioner and Custodian of the Vested Property and Non Resident Property, Munshigong reported in 5 MLR (AD)73 it was held that permissive possession of a party is not a adverse possession against the real owner. In the reported case, I find that the suit land of that suit originally belonged to Gobinda Chandra Dutta and others who had left this country for India some timing 1920 making over its possession daily to one Lal Mia who possessed the some for over 65 years without any interruption from any quarter. After his death the plaintiffs having been possessing the suit land for over 12 years and thus they have acquired title thereto by way of adverse possession and the defendants have no right, title or possession therein but they had most illegally enlisted the suit property as vested property, hence that suit was filed for declaration that the enlistment of the property as vested property is illegal and that the plaintiffs have title thereto by way of adverse possession. The vested property authority appearing in the said suit stated that the suit property has been correctly enlisted as vested property as the owners thereof had left for India and the government is in possession thereof through its lessee. In the trial the suit was dismissed by the Senior Assistant Judge but in the appeal, the appellate Court reversed the decision of the trial Court and decreed the suit. Against the judgment of the appellate Court below a civil revision was preferred in the High Court Division and this Division setting aside the judgment of the appellate Court below restored the judgment of the trial Court. Thereafter, leave was sought for before the Appellate Division whether plaintiffs' possession in to the suit land can be considered as adverse possession. The Appellate Division ultimately found that Lal Mia was always permissive possessor and his such possession cannot be considered as adverse possession in order to create title. The observations of the Appellate Division runs as follows: 

"Admittedly, the possession of Lal Mia, the predecessor of the petitioners was permissive. Lal Mia's possession was that of a licensee the possession of the petitioners who are his heirs could not he better than that of licensees. Permissive possession, however long cannot bestow title upon the possessor or his successors. It is fairly settled that when possession commences in a permissive character it does not become adverse unless by some positive overt act it is indicated that such possession became adverse either in the hands of the successors or even in the hands of the original permissive possessor. None of the courts below have found that there was assertion of hostile title to the knowledge of the true owners for 12 years or more. In the circumstances we do not find fault with the ultimate decision of the High Court Division." 

30. In the reported case Lal Mia and his heirs were in possession of the suit land more than 75 years but even then they did not acquire title in to the suit land by adverse possession as that was not adverse and hostile against the real owner and as against the government also. I find similarity between the fact of the reported case and the case in my hands. In the instant case, the defendants were allegedly inducted in to possession of the suit land as borgader of the plaintiff to borga cultivate her land. But, in the written statement it has been articulated that the father of the defendants  was a luxurious man and he did not plough his own land, rather he employing labors use to cultivate his land. So, he did not take any land from the plaintiff for borga cultivation. If the case of the defendants is taken as a fact that he was not engaged as borga cultivator in that event also since the defendants were allegedly possessing the suit land on the strength of an illegal Hebabil ewaz their such possession would not be adverse possession at any point of time against the real owner. But their possession had become adverse on 27.08.20(8) when they notoriously dispossessed the plaintiff erecting tin shed and wooden house on the suit land. As such, I find that the plaintiff was dispossessed by the defendants on 27.08.2000 and the suit has been filed within 12 years from such dispossession as required under Article 144 of the Limitation Act. As such, the suit cannot be considered as barred by limitation. 

31. The learned Advocate for the petitioners raised question as to the legality of the registration of the deed of gift in 1972 at Mymensingh Sub-Registry Office. As it has been found that this question of fact was not raised at the time of trial of the suit. So there is no evidence and materials on record on this fact but the fact remains that the plaintiff acquired title into the suit land through the deed of gift from 1972 and the defendants admitting the said deed took the land through Hebabil ewaz from the plaintiff on 23.10.1983. So, the defendants cannot raise any question as to the genuinely of the deed of gift of 1972. 

32. The learned Advocate for the petitioner also raised question as to the identity of the suit land as in his estimation there appears no identity of survey in the schedule Nos. l and 2 of the plaint. It is fact, that in the schedule Nos.1 and 2 of the plaint, the description of the land has been given articulating the khatian and plot numbers without mentioning the identity of the survey. 

33. From the plaint it appears that the plaintiffs has mentioned the plot and khatian numbers corresponding to the settlement khatian in the averment of the plaint but the same did find place in schedule of the plaint. However, in my consideration for this reason a suit must not be failed. 

34. The last point raised by the petitioner in this suit is that the plaintiff has claimed .30 acres of land from plot no.68 of khtain no.10 of mouza Kaida although the father of the plaintiff gifted on .20 acres of land from that particular plot. In answering this point the learned Advocate for the plaintiff opposite party no.1 submits that in an amicable arrangement among the co-sharers, the plaintiff used to possessed .30 acres of land from the particular plot. I find no logic to accept this argument, because them was no scope for having possession into .30 acres of land of that particular plot as neither the plaintiff nor her other sisters jointly got .30 acres of land from their father through the deed of gift in the year 1972 and the amicable possession of the plaintiff is a absurd story because the relationship between the plaintiff and the defendants are very much hostile in nature. So, in my consideration I find logic and justification in the submission of the learned Advocate for the petitioners that the /4- plaintiff cannot get any relief whatsoever in .30 acre of land from plot no.68 of khatian no.10 of mouza kaida. 

But so far the other materials on record is concerned, I find that them appears no legal 
impediment in taking the suit as a whole in favour of the plaintiff save and except the land of the plot no.68 of khatian no.10 of mouza Kaida. As it appeals from the materials on record that the plaintiff is a woman who got the suit land from her father in 1972 and when she was living in the house of her husband, the defendants who are nobody but the members of the same clan tried to grab the land in this or that way and as part of their said ill device they created a collusive and fraudulent Hebabil ewaz. dated 23.10.1983 and the plaintiff in order to protect her right and interest into the suit land filed Other Class Suit No.26 of 1985 and the said suit was decreed and against the said verdict appeal was tiled by the defendants but the judgment and decree of Other Class Suit no.26 of 1985 remained enact and the proceeding arising out of the said suit was ended on 27.01.2000. Thus, it appears that the plaintiff being a woman was in litigation with the defendants from 1983 to 2000, that is, for about 17 years for the suit land. Thereafter, whenever the plaintiff got the judgment in her favour finally in the former suit the defendants enmeshed her in the present suit dispossessing her from the suit land on 27.08.2000 and the plaintiff has been fighting with the defendants from 2000. By this time when the former proceeding was pending the defendants have created as massy as 7/8 documents in order to create more cumbersome and complication into the peaceful enjoyment of plaintiffs title into the suit land. The defendants left no stone untouched to deprived the plaintiff from the suit land creating obstruction and hindrance one after another. They have been chasing the plaintiff from 1983 involving her with the suits one after another encyclicals and the plaintiff has been fighting with the defendants to foil their such ugly brazen attempt to grab the suit land.


35. On a careful scrutiny of the impugned judgment I find that the appellate Court below rightly passed the decree in the favour of the plaintiff, but the plaintiff is not entitled to get .30 acres of land from the plot no. 68 of khatian no. 10 of mouza Kaida but she is entitled to get a decree for .20 acres of land from that plot. It pertinent to point out here that the defendants also admit the title of plaintiff into .20 acres of land from plot no.68 as it reveals from the Hebabil ewaz dated 23.10.1983, as the plaintiff admitting the title of the plaintiff into .20 acres of land in that particular plot created the deed. So, in my consideration, the decree passed by the appellate Court below may be affirmed subject to modification in respect of quantity of land from plot no.68 of khatian no.10 of mouza Kaida. 

36. In the result, the Rule is discharged. The judgment and decree passed by the appellate Court below is modified. The plaintiff will get khas possession into .10 acres of land in plot no.1452/85 of khatian no.458 and into .20 acres of land of plot no.68 of khatian no.10 of mouza Kaida and also into .30 acres of land in plot no.10 of khatian 106, into .09 acres of land in plot no.45 of -khatian no.108 and into .11 acres of land in plot no.49 of khatian no.108 of mouza Bajardi, that is, the plaintiffs suit be decreed for an area of .80 acres of land in stead of .90 acres of land. She will get the recovery of khas possession of the land specified in the schedule Nos.' and 2 of the plaint within the given boundary subject to the above modification. 

37. Let a copy of this judgment and order along with the lower Courts record be sent to the Court concerned.

End.
